title: Accelerated prefix coalescing and delta-encoded storage for embedding cache
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: Reduce end-to-end reranking and embedding-generation latency and cost by improving cache hit-rate and storage efficiency. This ticket implements a two-part system: 1) prefix coalescing at lookup-time to collapse near-duplicate prefix vectors into canonical keys, and 2) delta-encoded storage for clusters of highly similar embeddings to reduce memory footprint and network transfer. The feature must be tenant-aware, support per-tenant TTL/invalidation, and be compatible with existing prefix caching and shard routing. We will version cache entries with a content-hash header so downstream services can safely perform optimistic reads and rollbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Embedding cache memory usage reduced by >= 18% on benchmark corpus (news+docs sample)
End-to-end median latency for the reranking pipeline reduced by 12-20% under 95th percentile load
Cache hit rate for reranker prefix lookups increased by >= 7 percentage points on A/B test
Deterministic invalidation path for content-hash updates and tenant TTLs implemented and tested
End-to-end integration tests added; feature gates allow gradual rollout by tenant
No observable correctness regressions in reranking quality (>99.5% of queries within tolerance of baseline)
Operational dashboards: hit-rate, compression ratio, 95p latency, eviction churn added to Console
plan: Design data model: store primary canonical vector + delta vectors referencing canonical ID; delta vectors use packed int8 deltas with small quantization table
Add content hashing: use SHA-256 base64 for stable keying of normalized content; include model-version and embed-config in hash namespace
Prefix coalescer: implement a tunable LSH-like prefilter to detect near-duplicates at lookup-time and materialize canonical keys
Delta encoder/decoder: implement CPU/GPU fast encoder that computes residual between canonical and target vector and compresses using small-range delta-encoding
Shard metadata: extend shard manifest to include canonical lookup table and per-tenant bloom filter to reduce cross-shard probes
Invalidation policies: per-tenant TTLs, content-hash versioning, and explicit eviction API for downstream services
Storage layer: extend RocksDB schema (or chosen cache store) to store canonical -> delta-list refs and maintain refcounts for GC
Operational hooks: metrics, tracing annotations for coalesce/encode steps, SLO alarms for encode/decode errors
rollout_steps: Feature flag default OFF for all tenants; backend-only safe path available
Smoke deploy to staging with synthetic workload and end-to-end reranker tests
Enable for internal tenants and run 48h soak; monitor metrics and compare against baseline
Small customer beta (5 tenants) with manual enablement via Console; collect quality feedback
Gradually enable on autopilot for low-traffic tenants, then scale to high-traffic with throttling and fallback
Full-on by default after 4 weeks of stable metrics and no quality regressions
risks: Delta compression may introduce small numeric drift causing subtle rerank ordering changes. Mitigation: quantized integer deltas with baseline ABs and conservative thresholds
Increased CPU for encode/decode could raise costs. Mitigation: benchmark hot-paths and offload to accelerator if available; limit delta encoding to clusters above similarity threshold
Cross-shard canonical lookups can add extra network hops and latency. Mitigation: per-shard bloom filters reduce probes; cache canonical mapping locally
Edge cases where content normalization collapses semantically different texts (over-coalescing). Mitigation: bolt-on fingerprint salt tied to tenant or use stricter LSH radius for sensitive tenants
Complex GC and refcounting in storage layer could leak entries. Mitigation: periodic GC job with safety TTL and replayable audit logs
notes: We intentionally choose delta-encoding for memory-bound workloads where many embeddings are near-identical (e.g., page headers, boilerplate blocks)
Prefix coalescing is compatible with existing prefix KV-cache — we add a canonicalization layer that returns either canonical key or NO_MATCH
This work compliments earlier embedding-cache dedupe tickets but focuses on on-disk/storage efficiency and coalescing heuristics rather than pure dedupe TTL strategies
Estimate includes prototype encoder and basic Console metrics wiring; does not include hardware offload integration
